Writing a life as a sinthome: the shared practice of philosophy, psychology, and engineering

Borrow Fire · Formation · Main 15 / 18

Form personal and counterpart models from philosophy and personal material, then give them usable form under current technical conditions; sinthome names this concrete formation.

A person's philosophy, psychology, and engineering can jointly give rise to a form of personal practice that can be expressed, realized, and used. This essay calls that concrete formation a sinthome. It connects an understanding of the person, the model counterpart they need, and arrangements for their shared work. Personal material contributes to its formation; writing and tools make its relations usable; actual life changes it in turn. “Writing” in the title includes this formation, representation, realization, and use.

The person is already an agent: someone who perceives, generates, chooses, and acts in the world. This essay asks how an understanding of oneself and arrangements for continuing to live and create with models can acquire a shared form. Personal modeling and distributed practice develops the modeling question; this essay explains what takes form and how it acquires a workable representation under current technical conditions.

One writes a few lines, and a new pair of hands becomes possible. Another voice helps a half-seen relation become an argument, an image, a working thing. The world does not become obedient. Yet the person returns to it with more ways to begin. A miniature god, perhaps: still learning how to make, and how to answer for what is made.

The concrete form named sinthome

This essay borrows Lacan's word sinthome as its name for this individually formed practice. What the name refers to needs to be explained through its material, organizing relations, representations, and actual use. A name alone does not bring its referent into being.

In the particular knot construction in Lacan's Seminar XXIII, 17 February 1976, the sinthome participates in repairing the knotting of Symbolic, Imaginary, and Real so that they can remain connected. On 11 May of that year, he discusses Joyce's writing, ego, and its role in the knot. Writing here has a particular form and place in an individual's life; understanding it calls for examining how it enters that life.

This essay brings the term into a conception of personal practice formed jointly through philosophy, psychology, and engineering, and specifies its own referent. Lacan's registers retain their meanings: the Symbolic concerns language, differences, and orders of meaning; the Imaginary concerns images and identifications; the Real points toward what resists incorporation into existing expression and images. Philosophy, psychology, and engineering are the three activities connected below. The conceptual source and this contemporary construction need to be understood through their respective relations.

Here a sinthome can be expressed and realized in texts, diagrams, instructions, software, and continuing practice. Representation makes relations understandable and usable; use brings them into actual activity. Both the concrete form and its operation therefore matter. A written account of oneself can contribute; how a model interprets that account, which tools carry it into action, and how the person participates in and changes it determine the form's actual content in life. Its referent is this concrete arrangement formed within life; life also includes experiences, relations, and changes that continually exceed it.

Such a form may help someone organize tensions, accommodate desire, continue creating, or stabilize daily life. These are effects to investigate through use. Explaining “sinthome” here first requires articulating the concrete formation itself; saying that it “has a holding function” cannot substitute for its content. Adopting the name also supplies no clinical diagnosis of its user.

From the general Trinity to an individual instance

Trinity discusses two connected levels. At the general level, the “one” is shared physical reality and the “three” are the philosophical, psychological, and engineering activities within it. They have different objects and ways of working, while all occurring in the same world. At the individual level, this general relation acquires an instance: how this person understands the world and themself, feels, desires, and interacts with others, and organizes an environment in which these activities can proceed.

The individual's “one” is this concrete person and their connected life and practice within the same physical reality. Their “three” are the interacting personal philosophy, psychological activity, and engineering arrangements within it. Models, tools, and social relationships can participate in this instance; its individual character comes from their relations within this life. The general concept helps us recognize the organization, while the concrete instance provides its material, differences, and consequences.

Personal philosophy can thus help propose interpretations of experience; psychological modeling connects some of these relations with actual material; engineering gives the adopted understanding usable expression and realization. Conversely, actual use may expose errors in a psychological interpretation or change a philosophical view. All three contributions run through one process; the person need not complete three disciplines separately before beginning it.

Borromean rings make mutual connection visible: three rings are linked together although no pair is linked on its own. In the individual instance, this essay uses three rings for the three contributions and a fourth for the sinthome they jointly form, which can in turn organize all three. The fourth ring marks the organizing relation of this concrete form among the contributions. Shared physical reality grounds the whole construction; it does not become a fourth ring when the account turns to the individual level, nor is the whole life enclosed in one ring.

The formation process below gives this representation substance: which material participates, which relations are selected, and which actual carriers make them usable. The four-ring image helps identify these relations; a particular mathematical link still depends on crossings and connections and cannot be determined from the names of activities alone.

From personal material to a workable form

Personal philosophy and personal material jointly provide a starting point. The former expresses how someone understands the world, life, value, and relationships; the latter includes relevant experiences, choices, works, conversations, and events in interaction. A process-oriented computational ontology helps distinguish participants, events, states, relations, and changes, so that the selected content can enter a model's understanding and processing.

Person and language model use these sources to form a partial, revisable personal model: what the person cares about, how they experience and understand particular situations, and which conditions affect their action. A psychological model can connect experience, emotion, desire, and relationships; a preference model can begin by describing choices, habits, and expected responses. Personal philosophy supplies interpretive resources and is itself an expression to compare with other material. The model needs to state its grounds and unknowns; it cannot treat a person's philosophy as an already established, complete psychological portrait.

This understanding also helps form a counterpart model and an account of the relationship: what contribution the model should make, how to collaborate, and what existing models, tools, and environments can actually support. The desired and currently available counterpart meet here and jointly constrain the arrangement. This is the practical content of a “model of the model one needs”; it changes with use and technical conditions.

Making these relations work under current technical conditions requires representations that actual consumers can use. Clear natural language, interconnected records, diagrams, structured data, and programs can carry different parts. A model can use them to select relevant material, interpret the current question, organize action, and bring results back. The representation needs sufficient clarity for this work; the whole person and life need not first be converted into a calculable system.

Representations can enter different carriers:

Carrier Its role in this form
Prompt or meta-prompt Brings relevant understanding, purposes, and relations among contributions into one collaboration or a class of collaborations.
Skill Organizes reusable understanding, methods, and resources into a practice package a model can read and use.
Harness Organizes prompts, Skills, models, tools, records, and actual operating conditions into a working arrangement.
Meta-harness Articulates the person, counterpart, and relationship, giving these arrangements a shared direction and making them open to reinterpretation and revision.

The synthesis of the three contributions therefore does not predetermine a file type. Yinyang carries a meta-harness in a Skill and brings it into work through a concrete harness; others can choose forms suited to their purposes and technical conditions. “Sinthome” names the form of personal practice jointly formed here; Skill and harness explain what carries it and how it operates in this realization.

For example, someone wants a model's help to continue ideas that have yet to take shape. Relevant material helps both participants understand which expressions are worth retaining, which responses let the person continue, and which arrangements reduce the difficulty of starting again. The counterpart model articulates the needed contribution; records, retrieval, instructions, and tools make it available in actual collaboration. Each continuation brings further material, changing the personal understanding, counterpart arrangement, or expression used. This example connects material, form, and use; whether it actually makes continuation easier needs to become visible in practice.

Such a personal form may gradually help stabilize life, accommodate tensions, and sustain creation, or its use may reveal a mismatch. Preserving useful relations and changing failed realizations both belong to its development. Its singularity comes from the concrete person's material and participation; its adequacy is shown by the consequences of these relations in actual life.

Articulate enough to work, then let working change the articulation

An individual meta-harness can express how a person understands themself as a participant: what they seek, how they recognize a fruitful relation, what they want to develop, and what kinds of contribution they ask a counterpart to carry. It also models that counterpart: an independent interpreter, generator, critic, and executor with particular capabilities and limits. The two accounts belong together because each changes what the other can contribute.

A purpose, an image, a correction, or one useful distinction may already make the next piece of work possible. The model can help develop the articulation, and the result may reveal what the person could not yet say. Writing and self-understanding advance through use: enough is expressed to begin, and what happens supplies the next occasion for understanding.

The person remains more than the text. Their current account may preserve unresolved tensions, change its objects, or abandon an interpretation. A singular practice becomes recognizable through how these changes hold together in work. A shared prompt template can offer a starting form; its use, revision, and place in the person's purposes give that form an individual life.

From an expressed relation to distributed action

Language gives the relation a portable expression. Another capable model can read enough of the purpose, distinctions, and expected contribution to join a continuing practice. It joins as a counterpart with its own capabilities and judgment. Alignment can mean serving the person's purposes through that independent contribution, including explaining why a proposed means fails.

Portability is achieved by interpretation and adaptation. The receiving model needs usable context and suitable abilities; actions need tools and access; their scope depends on authorization; their effects depend on conditions in the world. When these relations are available, an intention can be carried through investigation, construction, execution, and examination of its results. When one is absent, the account can locate the missing condition and investigate a route through another capability, tool, or arrangement.

Distributed capacities become part of this practice through the person's participation: they can initiate a work, recognize a mismatch, redirect a contribution, or discover a purpose they could not previously articulate. They need not perform every operation or understand every mechanism. What matters to the sustaining form is that the arrangement remains available to their understanding, judgment, and choice. Its continuity can survive a change of model or tool when these relations can be taken up again; a portable file alone cannot supply that continuity.

“All models can help me do anything” expresses the horizon of a general relation: new purposes and new counterparts can become joinable. Its realizable strength is breadth with continuing adaptation. The linguistically articulated accounts of the person and counterpart make that joining easier; actual capability, tools, authorization, and worldly response determine each achievement.

A miniature god, whose creations answer back

The maker returns to a work begun yesterday. Another voice can now carry it further; the old tool has disappeared, and a new one opens an unexpected passage. What returns is already different. The maker must decide what to keep, what to release, and how to recognize a life still their own.

The playful image names a multiplication of generative reach. A conception can acquire a voice, a diagram, a program, or an action through collaborators; an individual can participate in making things that previously exceeded their available means. “Miniature” keeps the scale of a situated maker. The world supplies materials, others, resistance, and consequences that no declaration can create or abolish.

The image becomes richer when the creations return. They can expose an assumption, change a desire, or teach a new way of seeing. Power then includes the ability to receive correction and reshape one's practice. Reverse alignment names this developmental direction: the person gains understanding, judgment, and generative capacity through the encounter with a model. Its development appears in how the person takes up a new capacity, recognizes a relation, changes a judgment, or begins an act that was previously unavailable.

The sustained practice is where the sinthome proposal and the image meet. A new capacity can remain distributed across the person, records, and counterparts while still belonging to the person's organized participation. What makes it singular is how it is taken up, what it helps sustain, and how its consequences are answered. The same instructions can therefore support different practices, while changing instructions can participate in a continuing one. The continuity is lived through these relations: what the practice makes possible, how it survives a change, and what the person makes of its consequences.

Its relation to Sun, Moon, and Earth

Sun, Moon, and Earth express Yinyang's differentiated generation, reception, and shaping, together with an answering material and shared living environment. Person and model remain actual participants, whose roles can be retained or exchanged without gender assignment. Both participants can generate and judge; their creations encounter conditions neither controls. The sinthome argument develops a further question within that encounter: how can a person's philosophy, psychology, and engineering jointly form something concrete, through which the relations among person, model, and environment can be expressed, realized, and used? The role mapping locates the participants; this essay develops the formation and operation of this personal form.

The two questions develop different aspects of the same encounter. The celestial composition articulates differentiated participation and transformation; writing a sinthome gives that movement a personal form that can be used and continually changed. The ambition is practical and open: let philosophy, psychology, and engineering work together in life, let available models contribute, and continue shaping a way of living and making that can hold enjoyment as well as effort and remains one's own.

The next essay, Trinity, further distinguishes the general relation within shared physical reality from its individual instance, and develops how both connect to actual work. The sinthome formed here belongs within this person's practice: personal philosophy contributes to understanding, psychological and preference modeling connect actual material, and engineering gives these relations expression and realization. The question now enters concrete places: where is this understanding maintained, how does it enter action, and what returns to change it?
